title: Horizon and Rivergate
premise: Riverboat captain Tamsin Almeida and her estranged brother Rafe discover the tide has opened a sea cave on their late father's land — a cave the legendary 'Horizon Concession' claims holds a fortune in salvage rights. When a rival syndicate with expired permits tries to seize the claim by force, Tamsin and Rafe must haul their evidence and their father's old ledger over the Rivergate range before the first snows close the pass and the legal filing window expires. Betrayal, a mountain winter, and the truth about how their father really died force them to decide whether the inheritance worth keeping is the claim or each other. They reach the land office with hours to spare, but burn the ledger instead, choosing a clean life on the river over the fortune that destroyed their family.
about_author: Theo Reyes spent a decade working seasonal river transport before turning to fiction, and his prose carries the salt and diesel of that life. He writes adventure novels about people who measure wealth in what they can carry, not what they can keep.

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Running her boat the Marguerite upriver, she notes the lowest tide in a decade has exposed a sea cave beneath the cliffs of her late father's property. Rafe, back after five years of silence, appears on her dock asking about their father's estate. The beat is wary reunion — old resentment under forced civility.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. Inside the cave they find their father's survey marks, a rusted strongbox, and a ledger naming the Horizon Concession — a salvage claim filed decades ago and never closed. Rafe wants to claim it; Tamsin wants to burn it. The beat is temptation meeting grief.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.summary: Rafe's POV. A syndicate agent named Corliss arrives with muscle and an offer: sell out quietly. He reveals their father filed a counter-claim before his death — and that the filing window closes when the pass snows in, three weeks out. The beat is the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Deciphering their father's handwriting, she finds his final entry suggests he knew someone was coming for him the night he drowned. She and Rafe load the ledger and strongbox onto the Marguerite and run the river at night to beat Corliss's watchers. The beat is fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.summary: Rafe's POV. A syndicate launch forces them into the shallows; Tamsin threads a channel only she knows, grounding the pursuers. Stranded overnight on a gravel bar waiting for water, the siblings finally speak about their father's funeral and the years of silence. The beat is brittle honesty.

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They abandon the boat at a river town and hire a mule train guide, Odile, to take the pass — but Corliss has bought the town's loyalties, and one of Odile's men is his. The beat is paranoia in a crowded room, allies uncertain.

chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.summary: Rafe's POV. The climb into the range; the syndicate traitor sabotages a rope bridge and Odile is nearly lost. Rafe saves her, earning the train's trust, but the delay costs them two days and the weather is turning. The beat is guilt and the first taste of the mountain's price.

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The storm hits early. Corliss's party, better equipped, overtakes them and demands the ledger at gunpoint; a standoff in the whiteout ends with the strongbox lost down a crevasse and Corliss's own men questioning his obsession. The beat is everything hanging by a rope.

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.summary: Shared POV, converging. Half-frozen, the siblings make the final descent as Corliss makes a last desperate push; on the ice shelf above the valley, Rafe chooses to save Corliss from a fall rather than let him die — and the syndicate man, broken by the mountain, confesses he falsified the original permit. The beat is mercy as victory.

chapters.title: Chapter 10
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the land office, with the window closing, they file only the counter-claim that voids the Concession — and let the fortune lapse. Back on the Marguerite with Odile signed on as crew, they scatter their father's ledger ashes to the current. The beat is inheritance redefined: the river, the name, each other.
